snippet.title: Splatterhouse: Wanpaku Graffiti (Famicom, 1989) – Full Game (Secret Ending) Session 🎃🪓👻
snippet.description:
🔔 https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCMpNLYz8bcz1-i2vWxSEieQ?sub_confirmation=1     

*🎮 Title:* スプラッターハウス わんぱくグラフィティ (Splatterhouse: Wanpaku Graffiti)  
*🔄 Translation:* Splatterhouse: Mischievous Graffiti
*🕹 Platform Spec*  
 *🖥️ System:* Family Computer (Famicom)
 *🌍 Region Label:* JP 
 *📄 Revision:* Original  

*📅 Release:* 1989-07-31  
*🏢 Publisher:* Namcot
*👾 Developer:* Now Production

*🎲 Genre:* Action → Platformer ¹

🧮 Score Profile ²
 *⭐️ Personal Score:* B+ 
 *🌐 Consensus Score:* B (✓) 
 *💬 Cultural Impact (Ψ):* B– (▲) 
 *📆 Historical Tier:* B+ (✓)

*✅ Completion Status:* Full Game Clear
*🏁 Ending Type:* Secret Ending / True Ending ³

*🔥 _Difficulty Profile_*
  *📈 Difficulty Curve:* Gradual
  *⚙️ Perceived Global Difficulty:* Reasonable 
  
*🧠 Play Mode:* Focused / Optimized Play
*🎯 Intent:* Documentation


*Splatterhouse: Wanpaku Graffiti* presents itself as a parody horror film 🎬👻 brought to life. The opening graveyard scene ⚰️🌩️ sets the tone: *Jennifer* mourns Rick, lightning revives both him and the *Pumpkin King* 🎃, who abducts her. Rick’s journey spans seven themed stages—graveyard 🪦, sewers 🕳️, terror‑stricken town 🏚️, lakeside 🌊, campground 🏕️, manor on the hill 🏡, and the Devil’s Mansion 🏰—plus two hidden sets, a Japanese Castle 🏯 and an Egyptian Pyramid 🏜️.  
Each stage culminates in a *boss* that lampoons horror archetypes and pop culture. The most notorious is *Vampire Michael* 🧛‍♂️🎶, a parody of Michael Jackson’s Thriller. Others include Wani Zombie 🐊🧟, Diptera 🪰 (a giant fly evoking B‑movie horror), Frankenstein’s Monster 🧟‍♂️⚡, and repeated battles with the Pumpkin King 🎃. Rendered in super‑deformed style, these caricatures balance grotesque imagery with humor 😂, making the game both satire and homage.  
The adventure is framed as a staged production 🎥, confirmed by the ending: after the final battle ⚔️, *Rick* is congratulated by a director 🎭, only for the *Terror Mask* 💀 to twitch ominously once the crew departs. This meta‑cinematic twist positions the game as parody and prequel, since the extended epilogue (unlocked via the Crystal Balls 🔮) shows Rick and Jennifer approaching West Mansion 🏚️, bridging the comedic detour back into the darker continuity of the main series.  
What distinguishes Wanpaku Graffiti is not mechanical depth but stylistic hybridity: a horror pastiche 🩸 fusing arcade action 🕹️ with parody cinema 🎞️, embedding cultural references into every stage. Its legacy rests on this dual identity—both a cult curiosity 🌟 and connective tissue within the Splatterhouse lineage.  


¹ _Wanpaku Graffiti is best understood as a transitional hybrid, combining side‑scrolling platforming with proto beat ’em up loops. Rick can jump simple obstacles, but progression hinges on bosses and an experience system that rewards fighting enemies, making combat preferable though not strictly required. This balance—platforming diluted by combat, and brawler mechanics constrained by lateral scroll—places it alongside titles like Kung‑Fu, framed in parody style with SD horror aesthetics that set it apart from its arcade predecessor and contemporaries. Externally it is usually classified as an action‑platformer, but this label is more umbrella than precise genre._  

² _Wanpaku Graffiti earns a Personal Score of B+ as a clever, charming experiment mixing proto beat ’em up combat with platforming, offering originality and humor but limited depth versus genre‑defining peers. The Consensus Score of B (✓) reflects that critics and communities see it as a fun curiosity rather than a top‑tier classic. Its Cultural Impact is B– (▲): modestly received at launch, it grew into a cult favorite remembered for its parody tone and unique place in the Splatterhouse lineage, punching slightly above consensus. Its Historical Tier of B+ (✓) notes that while it did not found a new genre, it represents a transitional experiment in hybrid design at the late Famicom era, aligning historical weight with critical standing._  

³ _The game features a hidden epilogue often called a Secret or True Ending, unlocked only by finding two concealed stages and collecting the Crystal Balls. The first is in Stage III – Devil Town: after Diptera, enter the left pod to reach Secret Stage I – Trouble in Japan. The second is in Stage VII – Hell House: follow Pagan without attacking until a hidden door opens, leading to Secret Stage II – Sands of Evil. Completing both and securing both Crystal Balls adds an extended conclusion after the standard “film shoot” ending, showing Rick and Jennifer approaching West Mansion, providing the most complete and canonical resolution of the parody narrative._  

#SplatterhouseNES #Splatterhouse #HorrorNES

13:50 Stage Ⅳ - Diamond Lake
16:06 Stage Ⅴ - Diamond Campground
